taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-b-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-24, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1101.7 | 4.18 | 4.18
2 | 1144.4 | 12.44 | 16.62
3 | 549.8 | 0.62 | 17.24
4 | 173.3 | 7.65 | 24.89
5 | 2079.8 | 25.05 | 49.94
6 | 1111.4 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as KQHK-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-24, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

Station T-24 in survey area T presents a six-layer subsurface model. The resistivity profile begins with high values in layers 1 and 2 (1101.7 $\Omega$-m and 1144.4 $\Omega$-m), followed by a decrease through layers 3 (549.8 $\Omega$-m) and 4 (173.3 $\Omega$-m). A significant resistivity increase is observed in layer 5 (2079.8 $\Omega$-m), before decreasing again in layer 6 (1111.4 $\Omega$-m). Following the specified notation rules for consecutive layers, the sequence of transitions (K, Q, H, K) results in a KQHK-type curve. This matches the classification currently on file.

{"curve_type_stated": "KQHK", "label_issue_flagged": false}
